0.0.n: 日 marks the day of the month here, not a duration.

0.1.n: Placed after the date to specify the time of day.

0.3.n: This is a country name written in katakana.

0.4.n: Links Thailand to Bangkok, identifying the country the city is in.

0.5.n: This is the name of Thailand’s capital.

0.6.n: Marks the location where the meeting was held.

0.7.n: Passive 開かれる plus ていた describes an event that was ongoing in the past.

0.8.n: カ国 is the counter used for countries.

0.10.n: Paired with countries to describe the participating economies.

0.12.n: This subtitle token splits Ｇ２０; read it together with the following ０.

0.13.n: Completes Ｇ２０, the name of the Group of Twenty.

0.15.n: 相 means minister in this compact official title.

0.17.n: Combines with 銀行 to form 中央銀行, referring to a country’s monetary authority.

0.18.n: Part of 中央銀行, not a separate commercial institution here.

0.19.n: Names the heads of the central banks in this meeting title.

0.20.n: The preceding titles identify who takes part.

0.21.n: Marks the entire meeting title as what came to a close.

0.22.n: Polite past form of 閉幕する, used for the ending of conferences and other organized events.

1.0.n: Points back to the meeting’s closing mentioned in the previous sentence.

1.1.n: Together with その, places the next event just after the previous one.

1.3.n: This is the Japanese name of the newspaper commonly called Nikkei in English.

1.4.n: Links the newspaper’s name to its online edition.

1.5.n: 電子 means electronic, and 版 means edition.

1.6.n: Sets the online edition as the topic; its action appears in the next line.

1.8.n: This token is only part of Ｇ２０; combine it with the next ０.

1.9.n: Completes the organization’s abbreviated name, Ｇ２０.

1.10.n: The headline uses a noun alone instead of a full verb meaning the meeting ended.

1.12.n: This country name identifies who made the criticism.

1.13.n: Marks China as the source of the criticism in this passive construction.

1.14.n: Past passive form of 批判する, modifying the following phrase about interest rate rises.

1.16.n: Directly describes the interest rate rise inside the quoted headline.

1.17.n: Combines with 上昇 to name a rise in borrowing costs.

1.18.n: This noun describes an increase, without itself specifying a deliberate policy rate hike.

1.20.n: A one-character abbreviation used in the compact grouping 日米欧.

1.21.n: 米 abbreviates America here; it does not mean rice.

1.22.n: 欧 abbreviates Europe in the grouping 日米欧.

1.23.n: Marks Japan, the United States, and Europe as those moving onto the defensive.

1.24.n: Describes having to respond to criticism rather than taking the initiative.

1.25.n: Marks the resulting position; a verb such as なる is omitted in this headline.

1.27.n: Marks the preceding quotation as the title used with 題する.

1.28.n: Modifies 署名記事 in the next line, connecting the quoted title to that article.

2.0.n: This is the reporter’s family name.

2.1.n: This character belongs to 志晃, the reporter’s given name, and should not be translated separately.

2.2.n: Completes 志晃, the reporter’s given name; the subtitle splits the name into separate characters.

2.3.n: Placed after the full name as an occupational title.

2.4.n: Links the named reporter to the article carrying his byline.

2.5.n: In 署名記事, indicates that the writer is explicitly named.

2.6.n: Combines with 署名 to describe a piece credited to a named writer.

2.7.n: Marks the bylined article as what the online edition distributed.

2.8.n: Plain past form of 配信する, used here for publishing or distributing content online.

2.9.n: Combines with です to present the preceding statement as an explanation.

2.10.n: Adds politeness to the explanatory ending のです after the past-tense verb.

0.lit: 15th evening, in Thailand’s Bangkok, the ongoing G20 finance ministers’ and central bank governors’ meeting closed.
0.tip: 開かれていた modifies the meeting: it describes where the meeting had been taking place.

1.lit: Immediately afterward, Nikkei’s online edition, entitled “G20 closes; China-criticized ‘bad interest-rate rise’; Japan, US, Europe onto defensive,”
1.tip: The sentence continues into the next line: と題する introduces the title of the article mentioned there.

2.lit: Reporter Ueda’s bylined article, distributed—that is the explanation.
2.tip: のです adds an explanatory tone; the main action is already expressed by 配信した.
